chunks: Op-amp symbol and its two inputs. The question: Draw an opamp. What are the two input terminals?
The op-amp symbol is a triangle with two inputs on the flat side and one output at the point. The plus input is non-inverting, so the output moves the same way.
The minus input is inverting, so the output moves the opposite way. Supply pins are often left off the drawing, but they are always there.
Think of a tug of war over a marker that shows the output. The plus team pulls the marker up, and the minus team pulls it down.
Whichever input has the higher voltage wins, and because the op-amp's gain is huge, even a tiny difference moves the marker a long way.
The symbol puts minus on top by convention, but that can be flipped, so always trust the signs.
The triangle points in the direction of signal flow. The two input pins are on the flat side, the output is the apex, and the supply pins go top and bottom.
The signs are inside the triangle next to each input.
Inverting input (minus ): raising it makes the output go down. Non-inverting input (+): raising it makes the output go up. Output: the point of the triangle.
Supply pins: positive and negative power connections, often not drawn. Negative feedback: wiring the output back to the minus input.
Draw the triangle pointing right. Put a minus sign on the upper input and a plus sign on the lower input.
Add the output on the right, and optionally the positive supply on top and negative supply at the bottom. If the plus input is 1. 001 volts and the minus is 1.
000 volts, the output swings high. Swap the two voltages and it swings low. That is the whole idea.
"An op-amp is a triangle pointing in the direction of signal flow. Two inputs on the flat side: the minus input is inverting, the plus input is non-inverting.
One output at the tip. The output is the gain times plus minus minus.
So a signal into plus comes out in phase and a signal into minus comes out inverted, which is why negative feedback is wired back to the minus input.
I'd also add the two supply pins, positive on top and negative on the bottom."
